strengths: Deterministic SHA-256 selection with per-stratum scores and source hashes is a sound starting point for preventing outcome-driven cherry-picking.
The result schema is closed (additionalProperties false) and defines many required fields for requirements, ambiguities, and scenarios.
The validator checks duplicate JSON keys, path escapes, hash mismatches, and some count/family drift.
The methodology defines severity classes, recurring-pattern criteria, and a decision threshold.
The source-packet completeness concept and Lane B/Lane C separation are directionally correct.

findings.claim: The manifest is not immutable: the builder can overwrite it and the validator only checks that the current manifest matches the current builder output, so any input or builder change can be silently regenerated and pass.
evidence: scripts/build_correctness_audit_manifest.py: main() writes OUTPUT unconditionally when --check is absent
scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py: validate() runs build_correctness_audit_manifest.py --check and only fails if manifest differs from freshly built output
methodology.md: 'Changing any input requires a new manifest version and an explicit disposition of the old audit. Do not silently regenerate around an inconvenient selection.'
manifest.json has schemaVersion 1 but no audit version or disposition record
findings.failure_mode: An operator can edit a source index or the builder, run the builder to regenerate manifest.json, and the validator will pass because it compares against the new builder output. There is no git HEAD, lock file, or version/disposition check.
findings.required_fix: Pin the manifest hash in an immutable external record (e.g., signed lock file or git commit), make the builder refuse to overwrite without an explicit version bump and disposition, and have the validator check the locked hash and git status.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Change one selection input, regenerate manifest with builder, run validator; it should fail without a new version/disposition. Also test that editing builder constants and regenerating fails.

findings.claim: Pre-derivation artifacts contain semantic conclusions (disposition, physicalClass, equipmentStratum, batchDisposition, category, applicability) from semantic source indexes, violating the stated blindness boundary.
evidence: manifest.json units include 'disposition': 'base-competitive' for objective-mission units and 'physicalClass': 'ranged-weapon' / 'equipmentStratum' / 'batchDisposition' for equipment-starting units

scripts/build_correctness_audit_manifest.py: objective_sample() uses row['category'] and row['disposition']; equipment_sample() uses row['physicalClass'], row['batchDisposition'], row['disposition']; faq_units() uses unit['applicability']
methodology.md: 'Source indexes may locate bytes, crops, and versions, but their semantic projections, conclusions, named rule mappings, and conflict dispositions are not included.'
findings.failure_mode: A packet preparer or reviewer who sees the manifest can infer downstream semantic classifications before blind derivation, biasing Lane B and defeating the blind comparison.
findings.required_fix: Strip all semantic classification fields from the manifest and packets; keep only source-local IDs, labels, source paths/hashes, and raw excerpts. Move classification to Lane C reveal artifacts.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Inspect manifest and any packet for forbidden keys (disposition, physicalClass, category, batchDisposition, applicability); assert they are absent before derivation.

findings.claim: The 28 FAQ units are selected by a semantic applicability field in the extraction file with no independent lock against the source PDF.
evidence: scripts/build_correctness_audit_manifest.py: faq_units() filters 'if unit.get("applicability", "").startswith("base-game")' and asserts len(rows) == 28
manifest.json selectionInputHashes includes faq-v1.2-source-extraction.json but not the FAQ PDF hash
validate_correctness_audit.py does not check per-FAQ-unit sourceSha256 against the PDF
findings.failure_mode: If the applicability classification in the extraction file is wrong or changes, units can be included/excluded without detection; the audit population is not independently locked to the official FAQ.
findings.required_fix: Independently verify the 28 base-applicable units against a separate locked list or source review, include the FAQ PDF hash in selectionInputHashes, and validate each unit's bbox/sourceSha256.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Change one FAQ unit's applicability in the extraction file and regenerate; validator should flag population change. Mutate a FAQ unit sourceSha256; validator should fail.

findings.claim: Attack selection selects one occurrence per selected title, so source-different same-title effects are not independently audited despite the methodology claiming they remain separate candidates.
evidence: scripts/build_correctness_audit_manifest.py: attack_sample() selects 2 distinct titles, then for each title selects 1 occurrence from by_title[title]
manifest.json attack units show 'titleSelection' and 'selection' with candidateCount 4 for SCRATCH but only one occurrence selected
methodology.md: 'source-different same-title occurrences remain separate candidates'
findings.failure_mode: A divergent source-different occurrence with the same printed title can be missed entirely; the sample flattens same-title effects.
findings.required_fix: Select occurrences independently within title strata or explicitly sample across all source-different same-title occurrences; document coverage.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Create two source-different same-title occurrences with different effects; verify the selection method can select both or that the exclusion is explicitly justified.

findings.claim: Some component subpopulations are systematically excluded from selection, e.g., intruder-help bottom-row candidates are created but never selected.
evidence: scripts/build_correctness_audit_manifest.py: intruder_help_candidates() appends side['bottomRow'] with context='bottom-row'
intruder_help_sample() selects only strata queen-alive:corridor, queen-alive:bag-development, queen-dead:room, queen-dead:bag-development
manifest.json intruder-help units include no bottom-row context
findings.failure_mode: Errors in bottom-row effects cannot be detected by the sample; if they cluster, the decision threshold may be falsely passed.
findings.required_fix: Add a bottom-row stratum or document why it is out of scope; if excluded, state coverage limitation in the readiness claim.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Assert every created candidate stratum has non-zero selection probability or an explicit exclusion disposition.

findings.claim: Lane B sealing is not enforced: the blind derivation and comparison are stored in the same result file with only a whole-file hash, so the derivation can be edited after comparison without detection.
evidence: audit-result.schema.json: result object contains both blindDerivation and comparison in one file
progress.json rows have resultSha256 of the entire result file
validate_correctness_audit.py: validate_result_shape() checks packet/prompt hashes but no separate sealed derivation hash
methodology.md: 'The final structured answer is persisted and hashed before the reviewer can see downstream material.'
findings.failure_mode: A comparator can modify the blind derivation after seeing downstream material and update the result file hash; the validator cannot detect the violation.
findings.required_fix: Require a separate blind derivation artifact with its own hash recorded before comparison; the comparison must reference that hash; validator must verify the blind artifact is unchanged and predates comparison.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Create a result where blindDerivation is modified after comparison and resultSha256 updated; validator should reject due to missing/mismatched sealed derivation hash.

findings.claim: Packet content and completeness are not validated; the schema lacks required packet fields and the validator does not inspect packet files.
evidence: audit-result.schema.json: packetCompleteness only has reviewed, critic, findings, dispositions

methodology.md: 'every packet records: source files searched; exact included locators; search terms and neighboring sections checked; relevant FAQ/component channels checked; known exclusions and why they are irrelevant; packet-completeness critic findings and dispositions'
validate_correctness_audit.py: validate_result_shape() checks packet path/hash but not packet content
findings.failure_mode: A packet can omit a cross-cutting passage and manufacture a false ambiguity, or include semantic conclusions/legacy files, and still pass validation.
findings.required_fix: Define a packet schema with required search/locator/exclusion fields and forbidden content; validate packet content against it; enforce critic independence and resolution of findings.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Create a packet missing a known cross-cutting passage or containing a semantic conclusion; validator should fail.

findings.claim: The validator does not actually enforce the JSON Schema; it manually checks only a subset of fields and misses nested required fields.
evidence: scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py: validate_result_shape() checks top-level keys, packet/prompt hashes, ambiguities defaultProhibited, but does not validate requirements.citations minItems, scenario.then, discrepancy fields, etc.
audit-result.schema.json defines required nested fields and additionalProperties false
mutation tests do not include nested schema violations
findings.failure_mode: Malformed results missing required nested fields can pass validation, undermining the closed contract.
findings.required_fix: Use a real JSON Schema validator to validate every result against audit-result.schema.json; add negative tests for nested required fields.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Remove requirement.citations or scenario.then from a result; validator should fail.

findings.claim: The decision threshold is not enforced by any script; the validator only checks structural integrity, so a passing validation does not imply the audit passed.
evidence: manifest.json passThreshold lists criticalErrors 0, inventedAuthorityOverrides 0, hiddenDefaults 0, recurringDefectPatterns 0, maximumIsolatedMaterialErrorsInComponentSample 2
validate_correctness_audit.py does not aggregate discrepancies or compare against passThreshold
methodology.md: 'Stage 1 may support rewrite-readiness only after repair and re-verification if it has: zero critical errors; ...'
findings.failure_mode: An audit with critical errors, hidden defaults, or recurring patterns can pass the validator and be misreported as ready.
findings.required_fix: Implement a decision script that aggregates all results, checks critical/material/recurring/hidden-default thresholds, and blocks the readiness claim unless all conditions are met.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Inject a critical-error result and run the decision script; it should fail readiness.

findings.claim: Coordinated regeneration of manifest and progress can bypass all hash checks because the validator only checks self-consistency between them and the current builder output.
evidence: scripts/validate_correctness_audit.py: progress manifestSha256 is checked against current manifest file, and builder --check compares current manifest to current builder output
scripts/build_correctness_audit_manifest.py: --init-progress writes a new progress file with the new manifest hash
mutation tests call validate(check_builder=False) and do not test coordinated regeneration
findings.failure_mode: An operator can replace the entire audit population and progress with a self-consistent fake and the validator will pass.
findings.required_fix: Pin manifest and progress hashes in an external immutable record (git commit, signed lock file) and check git status/HEAD; require disposition for any change.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Regenerate manifest and progress together with altered selection; validator should fail without an external lock update.

findings.claim: Model provenance fields are incomplete and the schema requires a reasoning string, conflicting with the methodology's prohibition on retaining reasoning traces.
evidence: audit-result.schema.json: reviewer requires kind, provider, model, reasoning, responsePath; no tag, request mode, final response hash, or disposition
methodology.md: 'Record the exact tag, provider, request mode, packet hash, prompt hash, final response, and disposition. Do not retain or publish provider reasoning traces.'
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify exact model tag/request mode/final response; private reasoning traces may be retained in the required reasoning field.
findings.required_fix: Add required fields for tag, request mode, finalResponseSha256, and disposition; make reasoning optional or a non-trace summary; prohibit private traces.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Result missing tag/request mode should fail; result with a provider reasoning trace should be flagged.

findings.claim: Lane D independence and source verification are not enforced by the schema or validator.
evidence: audit-result.schema.json: verification has reviewer, sourceChecked, finding, disposition, evidenceRefs; no requirement that reviewer differs from comparator or that sourceChecked is true
validate_correctness_audit.py does not check verification coverage of critical/material discrepancies
methodology.md: 'A different reviewer or model attacks every critical/material discrepancy ... Its findings are advisory until independently verified against cited source bytes.'
findings.failure_mode: Non-independent or unverified verification can be recorded, and critical/material discrepancies can pass without source checking.
findings.required_fix: Require verification for every critical/material discrepancy, enforce reviewer difference, require sourceChecked true and evidenceRefs to primary source bytes.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Result with a critical discrepancy and no verification should fail; result with verification by the same reviewer should fail.

findings.claim: Recurring defect pattern detection is not automated, so the same root cause can be split or missed.
evidence: methodology.md: 'A recurring defect pattern exists when the same root cause produces material-or-worse discrepancies in either: at least three audited units; or at least two source/component families.'
audit-result.schema.json discrepancy has no rootCause field
validate_correctness_audit.py does not aggregate discrepancies
findings.failure_mode: A systemic defect can be labeled with different cosmetic labels and evade the recurring-pattern threshold.
findings.required_fix: Add a required rootCause field to discrepancies and implement aggregation that flags recurring patterns across units/families.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Create three material discrepancies with the same rootCause; decision script should flag a recurring pattern.

findings.claim: FAQ unit source hashes are not verified against the PDF, unlike component source hashes.
evidence: validate_correctness_audit.py: source hash check loop only covers rows with unitClass == 'sampled-component-effect'
manifest.json FAQ units have sourceSha256 but selectionInputHashes does not include the FAQ PDF hash
findings.failure_mode: A FAQ unit's sourceSha256 can drift or be wrong without detection.
findings.required_fix: Verify FAQ unit sourceSha256 against the PDF file and include the PDF hash in selectionInputHashes.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Mutate a FAQ unit sourceSha256 in manifest; validator should fail.

findings.claim: Concise-rule labels in the manifest are downstream labels, not source-local labels, and may leak conclusions to the blind reviewer.
evidence: manifest.json concise units include labels like 'Impossible instructions', 'Lander-launch timing exception', 'Contamination cards cannot pay Action costs'
methodology.md: allowed before derivation includes 'source-local IDs and labels needed to identify the selected unit'
findings.failure_mode: A reviewer seeing these labels may be biased toward the downstream concise-rule conclusion before deriving from source.
findings.required_fix: Use neutral or source-local identifiers for concise rules in pre-derivation artifacts; strip downstream labels from manifest/packets.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Inspect manifest and packets for concise-rule labels; assert they are absent or replaced with neutral IDs.

findings.claim: Mutation tests are not faithful to the threat model: they disable builder check and omit coordinated corruption, packet content, schema enforcement, decision thresholds, and status transitions.
evidence: scripts/test_correctness_audit_mutations.py: run_mutation() calls target.validate(..., check_builder=False)
tests cover duplicate key, duplicate unit, count drift, score drift, source hash drift, frozen hash drift, progress drop/count, path escape, pending attachment
no tests for builder regeneration, coordinated manifest+progress replacement, packet leaks, nested schema violations, threshold bypass, or status regression
findings.failure_mode: The test suite gives false confidence that the validator can detect adversarial changes.
findings.required_fix: Add mutation tests for coordinated regeneration, packet content violations, full schema validation, decision threshold bypass, and invalid status transitions; run with builder check enabled where appropriate.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Regenerate manifest+progress with altered selection and run validator; it should fail. Inject a packet with semantic conclusion; validator should fail.

findings.claim: No cross-seed deterministic control is present in the evidence, despite being required before final decision.
evidence: methodology.md: 'Before a final decision, also rerun ... cross-seed deterministic controls.'
No script or test for cross-seed controls in supplied evidence
findings.failure_mode: Seed-dependent selection biases or instability cannot be detected.
findings.required_fix: Implement a cross-seed control that reruns selection with alternate seeds and verifies coverage/distribution.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Run builder with alternate seed and compare family coverage; document expected variance.

findings.claim: Progress status transitions are not validated; a unit can regress or skip states.
evidence: validate_correctness_audit.py checks result status equals progress status but not allowed transitions
progress.json has no lastUpdated monotonic check
methodology.md: 'progress.json may advance only after the referenced result exists and its SHA-256 matches'
findings.failure_mode: An accepted unit can be silently reverted to pending or compared without derivation.
findings.required_fix: Enforce a state machine for status transitions and require lastUpdated timestamps to be monotonic.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Change an accepted unit back to pending with result attached; validator should fail.

findings.claim: The schema allows comparison and verification to be null for statuses that require them, and the validator does not enforce status-conditional requirements.
evidence: audit-result.schema.json: comparison and verification are oneOf null or object
validate_correctness_audit.py does not check that accepted/material-error/critical-error have comparison/verification
methodology.md: Lane C and Lane D are required for downstream claims
findings.failure_mode: A result can be marked accepted without any comparison or verification.
findings.required_fix: Make comparison/verification conditionally required based on status; validator should enforce.
findings.test_or_negative_control: Create an accepted result with null comparison; validator should fail.

missing_controls: Immutable external lock for manifest and progress (git commit, signed lock file, or equivalent).
Packet schema and content validator enforcing source-only content and completeness fields.
Separate sealed blind-derivation hash recorded before comparison.
Automated decision-threshold enforcement script aggregating critical/material/recurring/hidden-default counts.
Independent verification of the 28 FAQ base-applicable units against the source PDF.
Human-independent validation sign-off or documented human review gate.
Recurring root-cause aggregation across units and families.
Model provenance fields: exact tag, request mode, final response hash, disposition.
Status transition state machine with monotonic timestamps.
questions: Is there a separate lock file or git-commit enforcement mechanism not shown in the supplied evidence?
Are packet files and blind derivations present but omitted from the evidence? All manifest units are pending, so no packet/derivation content was available for review.
Is there a human review step planned outside the supplied scripts that could compensate for the lack of automated decision-threshold enforcement?
Are cross-seed deterministic controls implemented in another script not included in the evidence?
Does the manifest file continue beyond the truncated evidence, and are the remaining units consistent with the asserted counts?
Are the semantic source indexes actually free of semantic conclusions beyond the fields shown? The supplied builder usage suggests they are not.
Does the packet-completeness critic have enforced independence in practice, or is it only a manual process?
minimum_fixes_before_audit: F-01: Pin manifest/progress to an immutable external record and require version/disposition for regeneration.
F-02: Remove all semantic classification fields from pre-derivation artifacts and enforce the blindness boundary.
F-06: Require a separate sealed blind-derivation hash before comparison.
F-10: Prevent coordinated manifest+progress regeneration from passing validation.
F-07: Add packet schema/content validation and completeness enforcement.
F-08: Validate results against the JSON Schema with a real validator.
F-11: Add complete model provenance fields and remove required reasoning traces.
F-12: Enforce Lane D independence and source verification.
F-13: Add rootCause aggregation and recurring-pattern detection.
F-16: Add coordinated-corruption and packet/schema/threshold mutation tests.
F-03: Independently lock the 28 FAQ base-applicable units.
F-04: Fix attack selection to avoid flattening source-different same-title effects.
